articles.title: Drishyam 3 Reviews: Critics Call the Finale Gripping, Hail Ajay Devgn–Jaideep Ahlawat Face-Off
articles.excerpt: Critics largely praise the final chapter of the Drishyam franchise, with the Ajay Devgn–Jaideep Ahlawat showdown and the climax earning the strongest notices, even as some reviewers flag a slow first half and convenient plotting.
articles.image_caption: The official poster for Drishyam: The Conclusion features Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar alongside Tabu and Jaideep Ahlawat. Critics gave the Abhishek Pathak-directed finale an average of 3.5 stars across 18 published reviews.
articles.image_credit: Poster via Wikipedia (Panorama Studios / Star Studio18)
articles.nri_angle: For the global Indian audience, this finale arriving as an original Hindi screenplay — not another remake — marks Bollywood trusting its own writers to close one of its most beloved franchises, timed as the festive season's big family outing in cinemas worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vishal's Directorial Debut 'Magudam' Draws Harsh Reviews From Critics
articles.excerpt: The Tamil action drama, which marks the actor's first film behind the camera, earns a uniform 2 out of 5 stars across major publications despite a 185-minute runtime and a large-scale production.
articles.nri_angle: The Independence Day weekend is a major window for Tamil film releases that draw significant audiences among Indian diaspora communities in the US, UK, and Canada.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Odyssey Review: Nolan's Greek Epic Is a Spectacle Worth the Voyage — Mostly
articles.excerpt: Christopher Nolan's $250 million IMAX adaptation of Homer earns its epic ambitions with a stunning score and strong ensemble, even if some island adventures test your patience.
articles.nri_angle: Review of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, the biggest film of 2026, featuring an ensemble cast including several actors familiar to Indian cinema audiences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Festival Darling Max, Min and Meowzaki Finally Hits Indian Theatres
articles.excerpt: Padmakumar Narasimhamurthy's multigenerational dramedy about a Mumbai family, a breakup, and a cat named after Hayao Miyazaki arrives in cinemas after a four-year international festival run.
articles.nri_angle: The film's exploration of generational divides, interfaith relationships, and evolving family dynamics mirrors conversations in Indian diaspora households worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jana Nayagan Review: Vijay's Farewell Film Delivers Fan Service and Political Punch
articles.excerpt: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Thalapathy Vijay's swansong blends high-octane action with political messaging, earning mixed-to-positive reviews as a fitting curtain call for the superstar's three-decade career.
articles.image_caption: A still from Jana Nayagan, Thalapathy Vijay's final film released on July 23, 2026. The political action thriller marks the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister's farewell to a three-decade acting career.
articles.nri_angle: Vijay's farewell film is a global cultural event for the Indian diaspora, released simultaneously in five languages and reflecting the storied tradition of South Indian stars wielding influence beyond cinema.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satluj Review: Diljit Dosanjh Delivers a Career-Defining Performance in Banned Punjab Drama
articles.excerpt: Honey Trehan's biographical film about human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra drew 6.58 million views in 48 hours before being pulled from ZEE5 in India. International audiences are driving a 374% surge in app downloads.
articles.image_caption: Diljit Dosanjh, who stars as human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra in the biographical drama Satluj. The film was pulled from ZEE5 within 48 hours of release after government intervention.
articles.nri_angle: The film has become a cultural flashpoint for the Punjabi diaspora, with ZEE5 Global reporting a 374% surge in international app downloads after the Indian ban.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Heartstopper Forever Gives Netflix's Beloved Queer Romance a Bittersweet Farewell
articles.excerpt: Alice Oseman's feature-length finale trades fairy-tale warmth for a mature, emotionally honest goodbye to Charlie and Nick — and earns a 95 percent Rotten Tomatoes score in the process.
articles.image_caption: Kit Connor and Joe Locke star as Nick and Charlie in Netflix's Heartstopper Forever, the franchise's finale film (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The series' frank portrayal of coming out and navigating long-distance love resonates with diaspora audiences familiar with separation, family expectations, and building identity far from home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
